Context/Background:
Circular RNA (circRNA) is a class of noncoding RNA with regulatory potentials. Here, we identified circRMST as an exceptionally abundant circRNA predominantly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with strong conservation between humans and mice.

To explore the functional role of circRMST, we designed two shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction (BSJ), achieving 70%–93% knockdown efficiency. In 3D Matrigel-embedded cultures, circRMST knockdown significantly impaired cell growth across three NEPC and four SCLC-A models. Additionally, cell cycle analysis in SHP77 cells revealed cell-cycle arrest. In vivo, SHP77 xenografts in NSG immunodeficient mice exhibited markedly reduced tumor growth upon circRMST depletion.
Prompt:
To investigate transcriptional changes following circRMST knockdown, we performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells and identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes.

What are the most relevant pathways in a GSEA results with the differential gene list?  Nominate a target most relevant for neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
circRMST knockdown was achieved in SHP77 neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) cells using two independent shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction, yielding 70%–93% depletion. 3D Matrigel cultures showed markedly impaired growth, and cell‐cycle profiling revealed arrest. RNA-seq (shRNA1 vs control: 9,016 DE genes; shRNA2 vs control: 8,034 DE genes; padj < 0.05) provided log2FC rankings for GSEA. Replicate numbers and exact sequencing depth are not specified.

Keywords  
• GPCR signaling  
• mTORC1 signaling  
• Neuropeptide signaling  
• Cell cycle checkpoint  
• Unfolded protein response  

Candidate Genes  
ASCL1, GRP, CD24, SESN3, ITGB1, NTSR1

Analysis  
Across all libraries, GPCR‐related pathways—including Neuroactive ligand‐receptor interaction and multiple Class A GPCR families—are strongly downregulated (KEGG down ratio = 52.4%; Reactome down ratio = 66.2%). In contrast, mTORC1 signaling emerges as the most consistently upregulated module (Hallmark up ratio = 87.5%), alongside cell‐cycle (G2-M checkpoint, Mitotic spindle) and stress responses (Unfolded Protein Response). GO_BP terms align with suppressed neuropeptide and neuronal programs and enhanced ECM/fibroblast migration. These opposing signatures reflect circRMST’s role in sustaining NEPC‐specific neuroendocrine signaling while restraining pro‐growth stress–metabolic circuits.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
• Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction (KEGG_2016; NES = -4.054, FDR = 0.0136; DOWN)  
• mTORC1 Signaling (MSigDB_Hallmark_2020; NES = 2.679, FDR = 0.2103; UP)  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)

| PHGDH  | UP        | Serine synthesis enzyme, metabolic regulator  | mTORC1 Signaling  |
| TRIB3  | UP        | Pseudokinase, stress response                 | mTORC1 Signaling  |
| PIK3R3 | UP        | PI3K regulatory subunit                       | mTORC1 Signaling  |
| TCEA1  | UP        | Transcription elongation factor               | mTORC1 Signaling  |

Downregulated (Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction):  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                             | Pathway                                |
|--------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| GRP    | DOWN      | Gastrin‐releasing peptide                 | Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction |
| NTSR1  | DOWN      | Neurotensin receptor                      | Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction |
| SSTR3  | DOWN      | Somatostatin receptor 3                   | Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction |
| GABBR2 | DOWN      | GABA-B receptor subunit 2                 | Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction |
| ADRA2A | DOWN      | Alpha‐2 adrenergic receptor               | Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction |

Comparisons  
The consistent suppression of neuropeptide/GPCR modules across KEGG and Reactome underscores loss of NEPC identity upon circRMST depletion, whereas convergent upregulation of mTORC1 and cell‐cycle checkpoints across Hallmark and ORA highlights a compensatory stress‐growth axis. ORA also flagged ER protein processing, reinforcing the UPR activation seen in GSEA.

Implications  
circRMST appears to support NEPC‐defining neuroendocrine signaling via GPCR pathways; its loss triggers metabolic/stress shifts driven by mTORC1 and UPR, coupling cell‐cycle blockade with potential vulnerability to mTOR inhibition. Therapeutic targeting of mTORC1 (e.g., rapalogs) may synergize with circRMST suppression in refractory NEPC.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Assess the effect of mTOR inhibitors (e.g., rapamycin) on circRMST‐depleted SHP77 tumor growth in vitro and in vivo.  
2. Validate downregulation of key GPCRs (GRP, NTSR1) by qRT‐PCR and ligand‐binding assays to confirm functional loss of neuropeptide signaling.  
3. Determine whether UPR activation (XBP1 splicing, ATF4/DDIT3 induction) directly mediates cell‐cycle arrest post-circRMST knockdown.  
4. Clarify circRMST’s mechanism of mTORC1 regulation—evaluate DDIT4/TRIB3 dependency via knockdown/rescue experiments.
